features.label: // FEATURES
features.title: Built for players who run more than one account.

multi.label: 01 / multi-launch
multi.title: Start every client at once.
multi.body: Launch all accounts with one click, or only the ones you select. Breakbar closes the game's single-instance lock and opens the data file read-only. Your game files are never modified.

logins.label: 02 / separate logins
logins.title: Its own login per account. No passwords stored.
logins.body: Every account gets its own login file. A short guided dialog walks you through the one-time login and tells you when it was saved. Breakbar never stores an email or a password.
logins.alt: Guided login dialog: “Set up the login of Main?” with three numbered steps and a note that Breakbar stores no passwords.

switcher.label: 03 / instance switcher
switcher.title: Jump between clients from a small bar.
switcher.body: An always-on-top bar with one numbered chip per account. Click to jump to a running client, right-click to stop it, click an idle one to start it. Show it always or only while a client runs, lock its position, set its opacity.
switcher.alt: Instance switcher bar, floating over a plain backdrop, with four numbered chips: the active client, a running one, one that is starting and an idle one.

updates.label: 04 / companion apps & updates
updates.title: Your tools start with the game. Updates are guided.
updates.body: Start and stop Blish HUD together with the game, once per client or once for all clients. After a game patch, a banner names the accounts whose login needs refreshing and walks you through it, one after another.
updates.alt: Account list with a banner reading “The game was updated”, naming three accounts that need their login refreshed, and a “Set up one after another” button.

steps.text: Pick your Guild Wars 2 folder once, then add an account by name.

steps.title: Log in once each.
steps.text: The normal game login opens. Tick “Remember email/password” and close the client. Breakbar saves that login for the account.

steps.title: Press Launch all.
steps.text: Each account starts with its own login, side by side.

steam.label: // STEAM ACCOUNTS
steam.title: One Steam account, any number of ArenaNet accounts.
paragraphs: Steam signs in with the Steam user that is currently signed in, so one Steam account can run at a time, next to any number of ArenaNet accounts.

Steam only signs in a copy of the game that it installed. If you have the standalone game, Breakbar offers to link your existing installation into Steam. You click Install in Steam once, and Steam adopts the files instead of downloading the game again.
steps: Breakbar links your install into Steam
You click Install in Steam once
Steam adopts the files, no re-download

items.question: Is it allowed? Is it safe?
items.answer: Breakbar starts the game's own program with the game's own options and keeps a separate login file for each account. To allow several clients, it closes the game's single-instance lock in the running client. It does not change game files, inject code or read game memory, and the source is public. It is not an official ArenaNet product and not endorsed by ArenaNet; you use it at your own risk.

items.question: Does it store my password?
items.answer: No. Breakbar Launcher never stores an email or a password.

items.question: Does it cost anything?
items.answer: No. It is free and open source under the MIT license.

items.question: Why does Windows show a warning on first start?
items.answer: The first start may show a Windows SmartScreen notice because the program is new. Releases will be code-signed.

items.question: Where is my data?
items.answer: Settings in %APPDATA%\Breakbar, login profiles in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Breakbar. Deleting an account deletes its profile.

items.question: Can I run it from any folder?
items.answer: Yes. Put it in your own folder, for example in your user folder, not in C:\Program Files, so it can update itself later without administrator rights.

policy.intro: ArenaNet allows playing several accounts at the same time under conditions. In short, from their policy on dual and multi-boxing:
points: You may run several accounts, but you must play and control each one yourself, attended and independent of the others.
One keystroke or mouse click may act on one account only. No macros or input broadcasting that trigger actions on more than one account.
No bots or third-party tools that play characters for you or play unattended.
Multi-boxing is allowed in PvE only, not in PvP, WvW or other competitive activities.
Breaking these rules can lead to the suspension or termination of the accounts involved.
policy.note: Breakbar Launcher only starts and organizes the clients. It sends no input to them and plays nothing for you, so keeping to these rules is up to you.

sections.heading: Scope and controller
paragraphs: This privacy policy applies to the website launcher.breakbar.cc (Breakbar Launcher). breakbar.cc and the tools on its other subdomains have their own privacy policies; the one of the main site is here (in German).
The controller under the GDPR is Patrick Schmidt, Fischenzstr. 39, Konstanz, Germany, email: info@breakbar.cc. More details are in the imprint (in German).

sections.heading: Hosting with GitHub Pages
paragraphs: This website is served by GitHub Pages (GitHub Inc., 88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. Street, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA). When you open it, GitHub processes the server log data that is technically necessary, among them your IP address, the date and time of the request, the page requested and details about your browser. This data may be transferred to the USA.
The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR: I have a legitimate interest in providing this website securely and efficiently. More information: GitHub's privacy statement.

sections.heading: Domain name service
paragraphs: The domain breakbar.cc is managed with the DNS service of Cloudflare, Inc. (101 Townsend St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA). Cloudflare only answers the question which address belongs to “launcher.breakbar.cc”. The traffic of this website does not pass through Cloudflare. More information: Cloudflare's privacy policy.

sections.heading: Cookies, local storage and tracking
paragraphs: This website sets no cookies and uses no analytics or tracking services. Fonts, scripts and images are served by this website itself; nothing is loaded from third-party servers.

If you switch between the light and the dark theme, your choice is kept under the key “breakbar-theme” in your browser's local storage (localStorage) so that it is still there on your next visit. The value never leaves your browser, is only set at your explicit request (section 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG) and can be deleted in your browser settings at any time.

sections.heading: Download and external links
paragraphs: The download button and the links to the changelog, the license, the source code and problem reports lead to GitHub (github.com). As soon as you click one, GitHub processes your request, including your IP address, under its own privacy statement. The same applies to the links to breakbar.cc and slint.dev. I have no influence on the data processing there.

sections.heading: The Breakbar Launcher program
paragraphs: The program runs locally on your computer. It stores its settings, the accounts (names and paths) and a small log file with error messages in the folders %APPDATA%\Breakbar and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Breakbar. It does not store passwords or email addresses; a saved login is kept by the game itself in its own file.

The current version does not open any internet connection on its own and sends no data to me or to third parties. Should that change, for example with a check for new versions, this policy will be updated.

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right of access (Art. 15 GDPR), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18) and data portability (Art. 20). Where data is processed on the basis of legitimate interests, you can object to it (Art. 21). You can also lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (Art. 77), for example the State Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information of Baden-Württemberg.
If you have questions, write to info@breakbar.cc. The server logs of the hosting are held by GitHub; please address requests for access or erasure of those to GitHub.
